title: Folding a Christmas Paper Star
description: Shape a hanging paper star through its points, folds, and balanced outline.
cardDescription: Shape a hanging paper star through its points, folds, and balanced outline.
focus: The decoration combines flat paper and repeated geometric shapes rather than an addressed greeting or wrapped box.
solvingTip: Use shape clues before the folding words.
words: STAR
Pointed paper shape hung as a Christmas decoration
SYMMETRY
Balanced correspondence between parts of a folded design
TRIANGLE
Three-sided shape appearing in many folded star points
PENTAGON
Five-sided shape associated with a five-point design
ORIGAMI
Art of making shapes by folding paper
POINT
Sharp outer tip of the paper star
CENTER
Middle where the decoration's arms meet
CREASE
Pressed line marking a fold in the paper
ANGLE
Corner formed where two straight edges meet
PAPER
Flat sheet material used for the decoration
FOLD
Bend one part of the sheet over another
FLAT
Level rather than raised, as an unfolded sheet lies
ARM
One projecting section of the pointed star
THREAD
Fine strand used to hang the finished decoration

answerNotes.STAR: Stars can be made with different numbers of points and folding methods.
answerNotes.SYMMETRY: Symmetry describes a relationship between shapes rather than a material.
answerNotes.TRIANGLE: Triangular folds can form pointed sections of a decoration.
answerNotes.PENTAGON: A pentagon has five sides, while a star's outline has projecting points.
answerNotes.ORIGAMI: Origami emphasizes folding; not every paper-star design follows traditional origami methods.

title: Making a Christmas Pop-Up Card
description: Discover the tabs, folds, and paper steps that lift a small Christmas scene when a card opens.
cardDescription: Discover the tabs, folds, and paper steps that lift a small Christmas scene when a card opens.
focus: A pop-up uses connected paper pieces that move with the card's opening, rather than postal address information.
solvingTip: Separate the moving support pieces from the visible scene.
words: POPUP
Card design with a scene that rises when opened, two words
TAB
Small projecting paper flap used to attach a pop-up piece
HINGE
Flexible joint allowing the paper scene to move
SLOT
Narrow opening cut to receive a paper tab
BACKING
Supporting paper layer behind the pop-up scene
FOLD
Bend line down the middle of the greeting card
BASE
Lower supporting part of the raised paper design
SCENE
Small arrangement of festive shapes inside the card
STEP
Raised paper platform supporting a cut-out figure
GLUE
Adhesive fixing a paper tab in position
OPEN
Spread the card's sides so its scene rises
FLAT
Shape the pop-up takes when the card is closed
CUTOUT
Paper shape separated from its surrounding sheet
TREE
Pointed evergreen shape used in a Christmas card scene

answerNotes.POPUP: A pop-up card uses folds and attachments to make a paper scene move.
answerNotes.TAB: A tab provides a joining surface rather than the main visible image.
answerNotes.HINGE: A folded paper edge can act as a hinge without metal fittings.
answerNotes.SLOT: A slot and tab can help locate connected parts of the design.
answerNotes.BACKING: The backing supports the visible decoration rather than supplying its printed message.

title: Making a Christmas Paper Chain
description: Build a simple holiday decoration through loops, overlapping ends, and a repeating color pattern.
cardDescription: Build a simple holiday decoration through loops, overlapping ends, and a repeating color pattern.
focus: Each new loop passes through the preceding one before its ends are joined.
solvingTip: Follow the difference between a flat strip and the loop it becomes.
words: CHAIN
Decoration made from connected loops of colored paper
STRIP
Long narrow piece cut from a sheet of paper
OVERLAP
Place one paper end partly on top of the other
PATTERN
Repeating arrangement of colors along the paper loops
LOOP
Closed curved shape formed by joining a paper strip's ends
GLUE
Adhesive holding the ends of a paper loop together
TAPE
Sticky alternative to glue at a paper joint
PAPER
Thin sheet material cut to make the decoration
RED
Color often paired with green in Christmas chains
GREEN
Holiday color alternating with red in this paper decoration
HANG
Suspend the finished decoration above the room
LINK
One connected unit of the paper chain
CUT
Separate a narrow strip from a larger sheet
JOIN
Connect the two ends to close a paper ring

answerNotes.CHAIN: Each loop passes through another, producing a flexible hanging decoration.
answerNotes.STRIP: A strip is flat before its ends are brought together.
answerNotes.OVERLAP: Overlapping gives the joining material a contact area.
answerNotes.PATTERN: A pattern can repeat two colors or a longer color sequence.
answerNotes.LOOP: A loop becomes a chain link when connected to another loop.

title: A Christmas Package in the Mail
description: Prepare a small boxed gift for mailing through cushioning, address labels, and the post-office counter.
cardDescription: Prepare a small boxed gift for mailing through cushioning, address labels, and the post-office counter.
subtheme: A Christmas Package in the Mail
focus: The decorative gift covering goes inside a shipping box that protects it on its journey.
solvingTip: Identify protective materials before working on postal words.
words: PARCEL
Package containing a Christmas gift sent through the mail
CUSHION
Protect the gift with soft packing material
TRACKING
Service information used to follow a package's progress
CARTON
Sturdy cardboard box used as the outer mailing container
COUNTER
Post-office surface where a customer presents a parcel
LABEL
Address-bearing sheet attached to the shipping box
SCALE
Device weighing the package for postage
TAPE
Adhesive strip used to close the mailing carton
PADDING
Protective filler surrounding the gift inside its box
SEND
Dispatch the finished parcel to its recipient
WEIGHT
Measurement used along with size to calculate some postage
NAME
Recipient information at the top of the address
GIFT
Present protected inside the holiday mailing box
ROUTE
Path followed by the package toward its destination

answerNotes.PARCEL: Parcel names a packaged item rather than the card accompanying it.
answerNotes.CUSHION: Cushion is an action here: reduce movement and impact inside the box.
answerNotes.TRACKING: Tracking records shipping events; it does not promise a specific arrival time.
answerNotes.CARTON: A shipping carton protects the wrapped present inside it.
answerNotes.COUNTER: Counter is the customer-service surface, not a counting device.

title: Folding a Christmas Gift Bag
description: Turn a paper bag into a gift presentation using tissue, handles, and a small attached greeting.
cardDescription: Turn a paper bag into a gift presentation using tissue, handles, and a small attached greeting.
focus: A gift bag holds the present; tissue fills the top and provides a decorative covering.
solvingTip: Use a clue's material or purpose to distinguish the paper pieces.
words: TISSUE
Very thin paper tucked around a present in a gift bag
GUSSET
Folded side section that allows a paper bag to expand
HANDLE
Loop or grip used to carry the filled gift bag
BASE
Flat bottom supporting a gift bag upright
CORD
Narrow twisted material used for some bag handles
BAG
Open-topped carrier holding a Christmas present
PAPER
Material forming this reusable gift carrier
TAG
Small greeting card attached to a handle
RIBBON
Decorative strip tied around one bag handle
FOLD
Bend the tissue before placing it around the gift
BOW
Looped knot finishing the bag's decoration
GIFT
Item placed inside the holiday carrier
TUFT
Small bunch of tissue projecting above the bag's rim
COLOR
Feature coordinated between the bag and its tissue

answerNotes.TISSUE: Tissue paper is decorative packing, distinct from the bag's stronger walls.
answerNotes.GUSSET: A gusset adds depth when the bag is opened.
answerNotes.HANDLE: Handles may be cord, ribbon, or part of the paper construction.
answerNotes.BASE: A firm base helps the bag stand when filled.
answerNotes.CORD: Cord can form a handle rather than being tied around the whole gift.
